# v0.1.7: Radish study (sub-issue of #155)

Sub-issue of [#155](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/155).

The fourth external study feeding the v0.1.7 architecture refactor migration,
alongside the Drive9 study
([#157](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/157)), the Cloudflare
Computer study
([#158](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/158)) and the AgentFS
study ([#159](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/159)). It is
also the **Durable Objects placement study** the v0.1.7 persistence-scope
direction deferred: "Cloudflare Durable Objects is a future placement study
because its documented SQLite storage uses WAL"
([v0.1.7 checklist](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/README.md),
owner direction: implementation rules and persistence scope). This issue
commissions that study.

Radish ([Dhravya/radish](https://github.com/Dhravya/radish), TypeScript, status:
not production ready) is a **Redis-compatible server that runs inside a Cloudflare
Durable Object**: SQLite is the store, the Durable Object is the process, and R2
is the cold tier. A TCP-to-WebSocket shim (explicitly temporary, pending
Cloudflare's `connect()`) forwards opaque bytes; a Worker router authenticates
the upgrade and routes `?db=<name>` via `redis.getByName(name).fetch(request)` —
then exits the data path, so every RESP frame is handled by the DO's hibernation
`webSocketMessage` handler. One name is one instance: its own SQLite (10 GB
platform cap), lease and failover — "no cluster to shard, no failover to
configure, no AOF policy to tune — those are properties of the platform rather
than things to operate" (README). Values beyond the SQLite budget tier to R2:
`meta` never leaves SQLite, a hot/warm/cold state machine with SQLite-trigger
invalidation, upload-then-byte-compare promotion, and a pure-function eviction
planner; "every sequence fails toward 'upload again', never toward losing data".
Correctness is claimed through differential testing against Redis 7.4.11
(byte-level reply comparison), and the repo carries its own pre-repair
self-review (`REVIEW.md`, 2026-09-14, 27 numbered findings) whose repairs are
largely visible in the current tree.

The interesting shape for LayerFS: the LayerFS Store is also a single-writer
SQLite database, and
[cloud-sqlite-vfs.md](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.2/cloud-sqlite-vfs.md)
asks exactly the question Radish answers by construction — what changes when a
SQLite store leaves the local disk. A Durable Object is one candidate placement:
the platform (one-event-at-a-time execution, input/output gates, per-DO SQLite,
managed failover) owns the one-writer invariant, durability and failover that
LayerFS currently owns through `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE`, `journal_mode=MEMORY`
and a POSIX file lock. Radish is a full worked example of that substrate —
including what the application must still do itself (per-name authorization,
budgets, tiering, cross-store consistency) and what it cannot control
(journal/WAL policy, no pragma tuning, 10 GB / 2 MB row / 100-parameter
platform limits, no shared transaction between DO SQLite and R2).

## Goal

A source-backed breakdown of Radish:

- **Architecture:** the request path (client → shim → Worker router → Durable
  Object) as a diagram; the hibernation model (`acceptWebSocket`, session
  attachments with spill, alarms); the one-name-one-instance model and
  per-instance isolation; the deployment shape (alchemy IaC, bindings, no
  wrangler).
- **Implementation details:** the SQLite schema (raw-BLOB keys, `WITHOUT ROWID`
  per-type value tables, fractional list indices, nullable cardinality) and the
  fifteen mutation-invalidation triggers; `transactionSync` as the only
  transaction primitive and its three call sites (EXEC, fault-in restore,
  warm→cold demote); failure-ordered non-transactional writes; the hot/warm/cold
  tier engine (8/6 GiB watermarks, planner scoring with free-before-paid
  ordering and hard exclusions, promote/demote/fault-in, orphan collection) and
  the R2 bucket port; session/attachment budgets; the enforced platform limits
  (1 MiB values, 100 bound parameters, 100 KB statements, 16,384-byte
  attachments).
- **Interface:** the RESP2/RESP3 surface (incremental decoder, inline commands,
  Grisu2 double formatting, software binary128); the 124-spec dispatch registry
  plus 12 connection-scoped commands; the compatibility contract (pinned Redis
  7.4.11, deliberate deviations each pinned by a test, differential-testing
  methodology and its whitelisted relaxations).
- **Correctness posture:** `REVIEW.md`'s findings split into Redis-semantics vs
  Durable-Object-platform vs implementation defects, which repairs the current
  tree carries, and the untested-in-workerd gap (the whole suite runs on a local
  bun:sqlite adapter); the doc-vs-code discrepancies the study must settle
  (136-table vs 134-distinct command arithmetic, the 7,980-line claim, the
  HSCAN/SSCAN/ZSCAN expired-cursor asymmetry, the eviction trigger's dependency
  on TTL-armed alarms, unwired orphan collection, write-recency rather than
  read-recency in the planner).
- **What LayerFS can learn — the point of the study:** whether and how a LayerFS
  Store — or a split `StoreBackend` — can live in a Durable Object: one
  LayerStack per named DO as the server-enforced single-writer
  (cloud-sqlite-vfs.md D1-A/D1-C and invariant 2); DO SQLite's WAL against
  LayerFS's `MEMORY`/`OFF`/`EXCLUSIVE` policy and preflight WAL rejection
  (decision D2); the R2 tier engine against LayerFS's append-only `object_packs`
  region and the retraction contract (open questions 1, 6, 7); output-gate
  durability against "required encoding finishes before public success" and the
  no-retry owner direction; DO SQL limits against pack sizes and paged batch
  reads; the ingress question (fetch/WebSocket-only entry vs the daemon
  protocol, the shim pattern); what Radish's honesty artifacts (enforced-limits
  table, deviation-pinning tests, self-review) suggest for LayerFS
  documentation. These are recommendations handed to the v0.1.7 checklist, not
  decisions.

## Deliverable

One document —
`docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/radish/architecture_overview.md` (folder
initialized with this work item, including the study-lead handoff prompt) —
linked from the
[v0.1.7 checklist](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/README.md)
when accepted. It records the exact snapshot commit it was written against, and
carries its own diagrams in the repo's `text`-fenced style: the request path,
the hot/warm/cold tier state machine, the hibernation/attachment lifecycle, and
a LayerFS Durable-Object-placement concept map.

## Sources

- Upstream: https://github.com/Dhravya/radish (status: not production ready; a
  one-commit TypeScript rewrite dated 2026-09-15 of the 2024 Go implementation,
  which is preserved at tag `go-implementation`)
- Local snapshot: `/Users/yifanxu/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/study/radish` @ `98768e8`
  (2026-09-15, "Add a full-width source link mid-page")
- In-tree: `README.md` (architecture diagram, limits, tiering, compatibility
  contract), `REVIEW.md` (pre-repair self-review, 2026-09-14),
  `src/{worker,do,store,schema,session,resp,spec}.ts`, `src/commands/`,
  `src/tier/`, `shim/tcp-shim.ts`, `test/` (`differential.ts`,
  `local-server.ts`, `sqlite-adapter.ts`)

## Boundary

- Source reads against the pinned local snapshot only: no builds, tests or
  benchmarks of the studied repo, no changes to it, and no LayerFS code changes
  from this issue.
- The "not production ready" caveat applies: claims are checked against the
  code, not taken from the README alone. `REVIEW.md` documents the tree *before*
  repairs (2026-09-14): the rewrite landed 2026-09-15, so each finding is
  labelled with its repaired/unrepaired status at the snapshot.
- Cloudflare platform facts (WAL in DO SQLite, input/output gates, 16,384-byte
  attachments, 10 GB per DO, 2 MB row cap, 100 bound parameters) are quoted as
  repo-claimed unless independently verifiable; unverifiable behavior is
  recorded as unknown.
- Every load-bearing claim carries a source reference; performance numbers are
  quoted only from the project's own material with citations; this study
  measures nothing.
- Observations that imply a LayerFS change are handed to the v0.1.7 checklist,
  not decided here.

## Starting map (snapshot, orientation only)

A descriptive snapshot to start from, not a frozen scope and not a substitute
for the study's own source reads. Established by an initial four-agent
source-reading pass (2026-09-17); every line below is checkable in the tree.

```text
src/
  worker.ts        # router: /health + /connect; auth (constant-time compare,
                   #   fail-closed) + ?db= name validation; one-line data plane:
                   #   redis.getByName(name).fetch(request)
  do.ts            # RedisDO: Cloudflare.upgrade(); webSocketMessage/Close;
                   #   alarm() = sweep -> reap -> relieve -> rearm
  session.ts       # SessionExecutor: 12 connection commands, MULTI queue,
                   #   WATCH tables, attachments (12 KiB inline / conn_spill
                   #   SQL row), cold-key fault-in before dispatch,
                   #   promise-chain per-connection ordering
  store.ts         # Store: meta directory, lazy expiry, server-side SCAN
                   #   cursors, eviction candidates, byte-level glob matcher
  schema.ts        # 9 keyspace tables + tier columns + 15 mutation triggers
  resp.ts, dtoa.ts # incremental RESP2/RESP3 codec; Grisu2 (fpconv) port
  commands/        # 124 specs in 7 groups (string 21, keyspace 18, server 14,
                   #   hash 16, list 16, set 17, zset 22); synchronous handlers
  tier/            # engine (8/6 GiB watermarks, <=256 evictions/pass),
                   #   planner (pure function, free-before-paid), codec
                   #   ("DORD" header), bucket (R2 put/get/delete/list, k/<hex>)
shim/tcp-shim.ts   # TCP :6379 <-> wss byte shovelling; temporary by design
test/              # 624 test sites; differential.ts (seeded byte-level
                   #   comparison vs a reference server); local-server.ts +
                   #   sqlite-adapter.ts (bun:sqlite FakeSqlStorage; no workerd)
web/               # Astro landing page
alchemy.run.ts     # alchemy IaC: Worker + DO namespace + ColdTier R2 bucket
REVIEW.md          # pre-repair self-review: 27 numbered findings, 12 P1
```

## Status

Open. Created at owner direction, 2026-09-17; initialized only (study folder,
study-lead handoff prompt, informed by the initial four-agent source-reading
pass over the snapshot). The detailed study structure is written with the study.
title: v0.1.7: Radish study — Redis-compatible server inside a Durable Object: architecture, implementation, interface, and what LayerFS can learn
